check: verify the dedicated-biome entry's two factual claims, since it is the entry a reader is most likely to act on

claim1_thePackIsNORMALAndOptIn.code: OptionalTreePacks line 49 calls registerBuiltinResourcePack with ResourcePackActivationType.NORMAL, and line 51 logs the registration
claim1_thePackIsNORMALAndOptIn.liveEvidence: The stress log records it at 08:47:52: Great Wall biome data pack registered as NORMAL (opt-in) (plaincraft_great_wall:great_wall_biome).
claim1_thePackIsNORMALAndOptIn.verdict: Confirmed in code and observed in a real run, not inferred.

claim2_enablingItChangesTheWorldFingerpr.codeComment: OptionalTreePacks lines 34 to 38 state that the pack changes which biomes a world may contain, which changes the world recipe fingerprint, and that enabling it by default would make every pre-existing world refuse to load with a recipe mismatch. It ends with an explicit warning not to flip it to DEFAULT_ENABLED without accepting that every existing save becomes unloadable.
claim2_enablingItChangesTheWorldFingerpr.supportingImplementation: WorldRecipeGuard.fingerprint is used by GenerationResourceFingerprint and TreeBoundsCatalog, so the fingerprint is a real mechanism rather than a figure of speech.
claim2_enablingItChangesTheWorldFingerpr.relatedNote: The report records separately that BlockCatalog tag contents flow into the same fingerprint via catalog.hash, so tag drift is eventually caught by the same refusal - though it calls that a late and opaque signal compared with the direct assertions.
claim2_enablingItChangesTheWorldFingerpr.verdict: Confirmed. The entry's warning that a new world is required follows from this: an existing save would be refused rather than silently mismatched.

claim3_aRealRegistryOpsDecodeHasNeverRun.whatTheEntrySays: ForcePlacement was only proven statically; a real RegistryOps decode has never run.
claim3_aRealRegistryOpsDecodeHasNeverRun.consistencyWithTheRest: This matches the NOT_RUN status and is the reason the entry exists rather than being closed. Nothing found contradicts it.

whyThisEntryHeldUpWhereOthersDidNot: It names a mechanism, a consequence and a prerequisite - the pack is opt-in, enabling it changes the fingerprint, so a new world is required. That is the shape the other entries were corrected toward: height6000 lacked a real route and the Tan's entry lacked a reason.
